item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US-Präsident Donald Trump droht nach dem Scheitern der Handelsgespräche Kanada mit Zöllen von 50 Prozent auf Autos, Lastwagen, Autoteile und Stahl. Die Abgaben sollten ab dem 1. Januar 2027 auf diesen Wert erhöht werden, schrieb der Republikaner am Montag im Internet. "Wir brauchen Kanada nicht, sie brauchen uns." Die Gespräche zwischen den beiden Staaten waren am Freitag gescheitert, wofür sich beide Seiten gegenseitig die Schuld gaben. Trump hatte nach den gescheiterten Verhandlungen bereits Zölle von 50 Prozent auf kanadische Waren im Wert von rund 20 Milliarden Dollar angeordnet, darunter Wein, Möbel, Milchprodukte und Kleidung. Diese gelten ungeachtet des Freihandelsabkommens in Nordamerika, zu dem auch Mexiko gehört. Kanadas Ministerpräsident Mark Carney kündigte am Wochenende Gegenmaßnahmen an. "Man ist im Krieg, wenn man angegriffen wird. Wir wurden angegriffen." Sein Land werde die neuen Zölle Washingtons "Dollar für Dollar" spiegeln. Manager aus der Automobilbranche verwiesen darauf, dass Trump bereits früher hohe Zölle angekündigt habe, die dann aber nie umgesetzt worden seien. Da Januar deutlich nach den Zwischenwahlen in den USA im November liege, könne Trumps Drohung auch darauf abzielen, die Gespräche wieder in Gang zu bringen. Dennoch [USN:L8N44L18C TEXT:"stiegen die Aktien"] von US-Stahl-Herstellern und Aluminium-Produzenten. KLINGBEIL POLTERT GEGEN TRUMP Die Deutsche Industrie- und Handelskammer (DIHK) sprach mit Blick auf den Handelsstreit zwischen den USA und Kanada von einem besorgniserregenden Signal. "Eine weitere Eskalation und Ausweitung der Zölle könnte auch deutsche Unternehmen treffen, die in Nordamerika produzieren und auf eng verzahnte grenzüberschreitende Lieferketten angewiesen sind", sagte DIHK-Handelsexpertin Melanie Vogelbach der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. Bei den laufenden Verhandlungen zum nordamerikanischen Freihandelsabkommen USMCA komme es nun umso mehr auf Verlässlichkeit und Berechenbarkeit an. "Neue Handelsbarrieren oder anhaltende Unsicherheit würden das grenzüberschreitende Geschäft erschweren." So könnten Investitionen in die Region gebremst werden. Bundesfinanzminister Lars Klingbeil machte Trump persönlich für die jüngsten Entwicklungen auf dem Anleihemarkt verantwortlich. "Der Zinsanstieg der letzten Tage und Wochen ist Folge einer globalen Unsicherheit, die durch den Krieg von Donald Trump im Iran ausgelöst wurde", sagte der SPD-Co-Chef in Liechtenstein nach Beratungen der deutschsprachigen Finanzminister. Es gebe starke wirtschaftliche Verwerfungen, was jeden Tag an den Zapfsäulen spürbar sei. Der Krieg habe die Nahost-Region nicht zum Besseren verändert. Die Renditen für Staatsanleihen waren zuletzt in vielen Ländern - darunter den USA, Japan und auch Deutschland - auf den höchsten Stand seit Jahrzehnten gestiegen. Für Staaten wird es damit immer teurer, neue Schulden zu machen.

item.title: Cobre se fortalece después que cobre destinado a salir de la LME alienta compras
item.description: Los precios del cobre subieron el lunes ya que el aumento de órdenes canceladas o del metal destinado a la entrega en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) desencadenó una oleada de compras, mientras la fortaleza del dólar estadounidense lastró el conjunto de los metales industriales cotizados en dólares.
item.dc:creator: Pratima Desai
item.content:encoded: Los precios del cobre subieron el lunes ya que el aumento de órdenes canceladas o del metal destinado a la entrega en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) desencadenó una oleada de compras, mientras la fortaleza del dólar estadounidense lastró el conjunto de los metales industriales cotizados en dólares. * El cobre de referencia en la LME subió un 0,2% a 14.247 dólares por tonelada. Los precios de este metal, utilizado en los sectores de la energía y la construcción, alcanzaron los 14.396 dólares la semana pasada, el nivel más alto desde el máximo de 14.527,5 dólares registrado en enero. * Las cancelaciones están ocurriendo sobre todo en almacenes registrados en la LME en Estados Unidos y Asia —en zonas de libre comercio— y es probable que se entreguen a la Comex o a operadores y consumidores dentro de Estados Unidos, según fuentes del sector. * Los operadores y productores llevan enviando cobre a Estados Unidos desde que el presidente Donald Trump planteó la posibilidad de gravar las importaciones en febrero del año pasado. Las existencias de cobre de la Comex están en picos históricos de 742.778 toneladas cortas (673.836 toneladas métricas). * El zinc subió un 0,2% hasta los 3.829 dólares por tonelada, tras alcanzar su máximo desde junio de 2022, por preocupaciones por la escasez fuera de China, donde las existencias en almacenes autorizados por la Bolsa de Futuros de Shanghái se han más que duplicado este año . * "Una distorsión en la que tanto la oferta como la demanda se están reduciendo hace que el mercado parezca más ajustado de lo que justificaría el débil consumo", señaló en una nota Tom Price, analista de Panmure Liberum. * En otros metales básicos, el plomo subió un 0,6% a 1.909 dólares, mientras que el aluminio bajó un 0,7% a 3.214,50 dólares, el estaño cedió un 0,3% a 55.645 dólares y el níquel también retrocedió un 0,3% a 16.955 dólares.

item.title: US announces expansion of sanctions in 'economic onslaught' on Iran
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration on Monday announced an expansion of secondary sanctions it can impose on entities and countries that maintain business ties with Iran around the world as Washington significantly ratchets up economic pressure on Tehran with the war nearing its 6-month mark.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, Humeyra Pamuk
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump's administration on Monday announced an expansion of secondary sanctions it can impose on entities and countries that maintain business ties with Iran around the world as Washington significantly ratchets up economic pressure on Tehran with the war nearing its 6-month mark. At a press conference, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled what he described as an "economic D-Day" that aims to give a final warning to countries to sever their business ties with Iran or risk having key companies and entities cut off from the dollar-based financial system. "We are launching an economic onslaught against Iran’s financial connections around the globe. Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone," Bessent said. The U.S. Treasury Department has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil and evade sanctions and said that Washington would be working with U.S. partners to target any source of Iran's "illicit revenue." The department said it has issued determinations against five sectors -- digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping -- that the Iranian government is using to prop up its economy. The Treasury has also imposed sanctions on nearly 60 entities, individuals and vessels. China has for several years been the biggest buyer of Iranian oil and Washington has intensified its efforts to clamp down on Chinese purchases, but has so far stopped short of designating larger Chinese banks that may be facilitating the oil trade. Trump's war with Iran, which has pushed energy prices higher worldwide, is about to hit its six-month mark. While heavy fighting has subsided, diplomatic efforts to end the war have stalled and oil and raw material shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked, keeping energy prices elevated. Trump's approval rating has fallen to a low point, with just 33% of Americans in the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll approving of his performance. He says the economic costs are necessary to ensure Iran does not have a nuclear weapon. The U.S. has maintained sanctions against Iran for decades, most of which have been aimed at curtailing the country's oil revenues, aviation sector, cryptocurrency, procurement of weapons components and other military hardware, and cutting off funding for business enterprises controlled by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, a dominant force in the Iranian economy. The sanctions bar designated entities from the dollar-based financial system, but Iran has been successful in quickly standing up new front companies, other entities and vessel registrations to evade the sanctions.

item.title: Coinbase-backed crypto advocacy group endorses 32 US midterm candidates
item.description: The endorsements come as the Clarity Act, the crypto industry's top policy priority, stalls in the Senate amid opposition from some lawmakers.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Lang
item.content:encoded: Stand With Crypto, an advocacy group backed by crypto giant Coinbase (COIN.O) , on Monday endorsed 32 incumbent congressional candidates for the November midterm elections, as the industry cements influence in Washington. The endorsements, first reported by Reuters, come as the Clarity Act, the crypto industry's top policy priority, stalls in the Senate amid opposition from some lawmakers. All the candidates endorsed voted last year to pass the bill out of the House of Representatives, and Stand With Crypto hopes to return those industry-friendly candidates to office. Crypto companies say the legislation would give them long-sought legal clarity. Stand With Crypto's 2026 campaign builds on its 2024 effort, the first cycle that the group was active, Mason Lynaugh, executive director of Stand With Crypto, said in an interview. "In 2024 we were very much proving that the crypto voter is real. In 2026 we're very much showing that we have the organizing capacity and that our advocates are a true voting bloc that can move the needle," said Lynaugh. Coinbase [USN:L1N3AU25A TEXT:"launched Stand With Crypto in 2023"] to jumpstart a grassroots advocacy campaign with the goal of advancing pro-crypto legislation. It aims to influence elections by organizing and mobilizing voters rather than through large campaign expenditures. It says it has more than 3 million registered U.S. "advocates." Stand With Crypto endorsed six congressional candidates in March who are running for reelection. Among the new raft of 32 endorsees are some of the industry's key House allies, including Republicans Tom Emmer, and Bill Huizenga, and Democrats Ritchie Torres and Josh Gottheimer. Several of the 32 are running in competitive races, like Arizona Republican Juan Ciscomani and Pennsylvania Republican Brian Fitzpatrick. "I think we can be the difference maker in some of these," Lynaugh said. The group said it will announce its Senate endorsements closer to Election Day. The crypto industry [USN:L1N4310KM TEXT:"spent $170 million"] supporting congressional candidates during the 2024 elections, many of whom won their races. That helped it score a victory last year when Congress passed the Genius Act, which created rules for dollar-backed crypto tokens called stablecoins, potentially boosting their adoption. The sector has already [USN:L1N43P0YD TEXT:"poured close to $200 million"] into the November midterm elections, underscoring its muscle in Congress. Much of that has been directed through Fairshake, a major super political action committee created to support pro-crypto candidates.

item.title: Paraná já planta milho 1ª safra de olho no El Niño, umidade limita avanço no RS, diz AgRural
item.description: O plantio de milho primeira safra da nova temporada 2026/27 teve um início mais antecipado no Paraná, com produtores se precavendo de eventuais chuvas excessivas associadas ao El Niño no Sul do Brasil, enquanto no Rio Grande do Sul a umidade ainda limita maiores avanços, afirmou nesta segunda-feira a AgRural.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O plantio de milho primeira safra da nova temporada 2026/27 teve um início mais antecipado no Paraná, com produtores se precavendo de eventuais chuvas excessivas associadas ao El Niño no Sul do Brasil, enquanto no Rio Grande do Sul a umidade ainda limita maiores avanços, afirmou nesta segunda-feira a AgRural. Neste contexto, a área plantada no centro-sul brasileiro havia atingido até a última quinta-feira 2% dos 2,8 milhões de hectares previstos, ante 0,3% uma semana antes e 3,2% um ano atrás, quando a principal região produtora semeou 2,7 milhões de hectares. "No Paraná, o início do plantio está com ritmo à frente do ano passado e da média, com produtores antecipando para desviar de possíveis chuvas mais frequentes em setembro", afirmou o analista da AgRural Adriano Gomes. Por outro lado, no Rio Grande do Sul a umidade ainda limita o avanço da semeadura, de acordo com a consultoria, que registra também as plantadeiras percorrendo os campos de Santa Catarina. O Rio Grande do Sul, que não faz segunda safra, é o principal produtor de milho primeira safra do país, enquanto o Paraná foi o terceiro maior na colheita do cereal de verão no ciclo passado, atrás de Minas Gerais, segundo dados da Conab. Projetando um aumento de 3,7% na área plantada com milho primeira safra 2026/27 do centro-sul, na comparação com a estimativa da Conab, a AgRural estima um crescimento na produção de 1,8%, para 22,8 milhões de toneladas, considerando uma linha de tendência para a produtividade. A maior parte da produção de milho do Brasil é obtida na segunda safra. Em 2025/26, segundo números da Conab, ela deve representar 78% do total. COLHEITA 25/26 PERTO DO FINAL A colheita de milho segunda safra na região centro-sul do Brasil no ciclo 2025/26 atingiu 92% da área até a última quinta-feira, avançando [USN:S0N44906Q TEXT:"7 pontos percentuais"] frente à semana anterior e contra 98% registrados um ano atrás, segundo levantamento da AgRural divulgado nesta segunda-feira. Em nota, a consultoria afirmou que os trabalhos estão encerrados em Mato Grosso e muito próximos do fim em Goiás e Minas Gerais, enquanto no Paraná "o ritmo melhorou, mas a umidade ainda mantém a colheita mais lenta que o normal".

item.title: Merz empfängt in Finanzdebatte EU-Nettozahler im Kanzleramt

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz hat mehrere EU-Staats- und Regierungschefs eingeladen, um sich in der laufenden Debatte über die künftigen EU-Finanzen abzustimmen. Teilnehmen sollten Vertreter aus Dänemark, Österreich, Finnland und den Niederlanden, sagte Regierungssprecher Stefan Kornelius am Montag in Berlin. Es sei allerdings noch nicht klar, ob diese Liste bereits abschließend sei. Das Treffen soll am Donnerstagmittag im Kanzleramt stattfinden. Eingeladen seien Länder, die das Ziel teilten, dass der sogenannte EU-Finanzrahmen für die Jahre 2028 bis 2034 noch in diesem Jahr abgeschlossen werden solle, hieß es weiter. Es handelt sich zudem um Nettozahlerstaaten, also Länder, die mehr Geld nach Brüssel überweisen, als sie über Programme und Subventionen zurückbekommen. Frankreichs Präsident Emmanuel Macron werde nicht kommen, aber mit ihm habe Merz bereits eine sehr enge Abstimmung bei dem Thema, sagte der Regierungssprecher. Kornelius verwies auf die Position des Kanzlers, dass der bisher vorliegende Budgetentwurf "in allen Bereichen, und zwar um mehrere hundert Milliarden Euro" gekürzt werden müsse. Die Regierung fordert ein Abspecken der EU-Kommissionsvorschläge von zwei Billionen Euro auf 1,6 Billionen Euro für die siebenjährige Periode. Man müsse sehen, wie weit man mit den neuen EU-Eigenmitteln komme, also eigenen Einnahmequellen der EU. Zudem müssten die neuen politischen Prioritäten im Finanzrahmen abgebildet werden. "Das ist der Rahmen, in dem auch verhandelt oder gesprochen wird", betonte Merz. Hintergrund ist zum einen, dass die Bundesregierung auf eine Neuausrichtung der EU-Finanzen pocht, in der Subventionen für die Landwirtschaft und sogenannte Regionalmittel zugunsten von Verteidigungs- und Forschungsausgaben umgeschichtet werden sollen. Zum anderen sorgt sie sich, dass die Kommissionsvorschläge zu zu hohen jährlichen Überweisungen nach Brüssel führen könnten. "Das würde bedeuten, dass Deutschland zwischen 15 und 20 Milliarden Euro zusätzlich jedes Jahr in die Kasse der Europäischen Union einzahlen müsste. Das können wir nicht", hatte Merz schon im Juni betont. Der Kanzler hatte darüber auch im Juli bei einem Besuch in Irland gesprochen, das derzeit die EU-Ratspräsidentschaft innehat und in dieser Funktion wahrscheinlich im Oktober ein neues Finanztableau vorlegen soll. Deutschland und Frankreich drängen auf einen Abschluss noch in diesem Jahr. Grund ist auch, dass wegen wichtiger Wahlen in Frankreich, Polen und Italien im kommenden Jahr kein Abschluss erwartet wird.

item.title: Miners support FTSE 100 as investors eye key events
item.description: The UK's FTSE 100 index edged higher on Monday, as miners helped offset geopolitical tensions, while investors braced for big-ticket events that could set the tone for global markets in the near term.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The UK's FTSE 100 index edged higher on Monday, as miners helped offset geopolitical tensions, while investors braced for big-ticket events that could set the tone for global markets in the near term. The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) rose 0.4% to 10,854.32 points, while the midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) was flat at 24,717.48 points. Investors are awaiting [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"details"] on new U.S. sanctions targeting Iran's trade partners by calling it "the greatest financial offensive ever", which could disrupt crude supplies from the Middle East. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to hold a press conference later in the day to outline the sanctions. Washington says Iran must relinquish its control over the vital Strait of Hormuz, a route that once carried a fifth of global supplies. Oil prices , eased ahead of the announcement, dragging down British energy major BP (BP.L) by 2.9%. On the flipside, miners Rio Tinto (RIO.L) and Anglo American (AAL.L) gained 0.3% and 1.3%, respectively, as a weaker U.S. currency supported metal prices. This week, investors will keep a close watch on chipmaker Nvidia's (NVDA.O) earnings, seen as a major test of the AI rally that has been a key driver pushing stocks to record highs. U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's debut speech at the annual Jackson Hole conference this week will also be on traders' radar as they seek guidance about the recent jump in bond yields and monetary policy outlook. Consumer stocks British American Tobacco (BATS.L) , Diageo (DGE.L) and Unilever (ULVR.L) were higher, offering support to the main index. Shell (SHEL.L) has drawn interest from potential bidders, including ExxonMobil (XOM.N) and LyondellBasell (LYB.N) , for its U.S. chemical assets that could fetch up to $8 billion, the Financial Times reported. Shell's stock dipped in line with oil prices. Shares of transport tech company Tracsis (TRCS.L) rose 4.7% after raising its full-year forecasts.

item.title: Dólar sube ligeramente y dólar canadiense cae tras anuncio de aranceles por parte de EEUU
item.description: El dólar subía ligeramente el lunes tras registrar su tercera caída semanal de las últimas cuatro, lo que llevó a la moneda a mínimos de tres meses, mientras el Tesoro estadounidense se comprometía a recomprar más bonos a largo plazo y se esperaban detalles sobre las sanciones a Irán.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
item.content:encoded: El dólar subía ligeramente el lunes tras registrar su tercera caída semanal de las últimas cuatro, lo que llevó a la moneda a mínimos de tres meses, mientras el Tesoro estadounidense se comprometía a recomprar más bonos a largo plazo y se esperaban detalles sobre las sanciones a Irán. * Tras el anuncio de la semana pasada por parte del Departamento del Tesoro de que duplicaría el volumen de las operaciones de recompra, la CNBC informó el lunes, citando a altos funcionarios del Tesoro, que el secretario Scott Bessent podría recurrir a la Cuenta General del departamento, de casi 1 billón de dólares, para ayudar a financiar las recompras de bonos en lugar de emitir letras a corto plazo. * El dólar recortaba parte de sus ganancias tras la noticia, al igual que los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro a más largo plazo. * "Si es cierta la noticia de que el Tesoro va a anunciar que utilizará una parte de su Cuenta General del Tesoro en la Fed para comprar bonos a más largo plazo, podría ser un experimento interesante. ¿Funciona disparar un bazuca contra un huracán?", dijo Brian Jacobsen, economista jefe de Annex Wealth Management en Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin. * "Unos rendimientos más bajos en los bonos a largo plazo no resolverán el problema de la deuda. A largo plazo, podrían empeorarlo. La carga de la deuda pública se volvería aún más sensible a los cambios en la tasa de interés oficial de la Fed". * El índice dólar subía un 0,11% a 98,94 mientras que el euro bajaba un 0,07% a 1,1671 dólares. * Por otra parte, ls tensiones comerciales lastraban al dólar canadiense , que se debilitaba un 0,41 % -su mayor caída desde el 17 de junio- frente a su par estadounidense, hasta situarse en 1,382 dólares canadienses por dólar. * La moneda se encaminaba a romper una racha de tres días de ganancias, después de que Washington impusiera aranceles del 50% a los productos canadienses, ante lo cual Canadá prometió tomar represalias "dólar por dólar" contra los nuevos gravámenes. * El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmó el lunes en una publicación en redes sociales que los aranceles sobre todos los automóviles y camiones, las piezas de automóvil y el acero se incrementarán hasta el 50% a partir del 1 de enero de 2027. * La libra esterlina subía ligeramente un 0,03% a 1,3644 dólares, manteniéndose cerca de su máximo de seis meses de 1,3675 dólares del viernes. El yen japonés se depreciaba un 0,11% frente al dólar, a 159,13 por dólar.

item.title: Grid bottlenecks push businesses toward larger onsite power systems, Capstone says
item.description: Rising demand for onsite power among businesses struggling to secure capacity from strained American utilities is propelling orders for larger generation blocks at Capstone Energy+ , CEO Vince Canino said in an interview with Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Arunima Kumar
item.content:encoded: Rising demand for onsite power among businesses struggling to secure capacity from strained American utilities is propelling orders for larger generation blocks at Capstone Energy+ (CEPL.O) , CEO Vince Canino said in an interview with Reuters. As grid constraints grow, businesses are increasingly viewing onsite generation as a way to secure power for expansion rather than simply a means of reducing energy costs. Capstone, which provides microturbine and behind-the-meter power systems for commercial and industrial customers, is seeing demand from sectors including healthcare and is pursuing data-center projects. "Today's discussions are truly about energy certainty," Canino said. Capstone is now seeing customers buy larger blocks of power, including 3, 4 and 6-megawatt systems, compared with smaller projects that were more typical in the past, Canino said. A 1-megawatt power system can typically supply electricity to roughly 750-1,000 homes at a given time, depending on average household demand and location. Customers are also moving faster to secure onsite power as they face delays in obtaining utility capacity. "I think today a lot of those cycles are shrinking because it's no longer about, well, is this a really good investment and what's the return? It's more about I need power and I've got to make sure I have it on demand," Canino said. Capstone recently installed a 2 MW combined heat and power system at Scripps Mercy Hospital in San Diego, providing electricity and backup power during outages. The company has deployed its technology at small enterprise data centers but has yet to deploy it at a large-scale data center, Canino said.

item.title: U.S. court orders Guardant to pay $245 million in DNA sequencing patent dispute
item.description: A U.S. court has ordered Guardant Health to pay more than $245.2 million to TwinStrand Biosciences and the University of Washington after finding that the company infringed patents covering DNA sequencing technology, TwinStrand said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A U.S. court has ordered Guardant Health to pay more than $245.2 million to TwinStrand Biosciences and the University of Washington after finding that the company infringed patents covering DNA sequencing technology, TwinStrand said on Monday. Here are the details: The U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware entered final judgment on August 21, upholding a [USN:L1N3CG1HD TEXT:"2023 jury verdict"] that found Guardant had willfully infringed two patents related to TwinStrand's DNA sequencing technology. "We strongly disagree with this decision and will promptly be appealing for its overturn," said John Saia, Guardant's Chief Legal Officer. "We have full faith in the strengths and merits of Guardant’s intellectual property and R&D and are confident we will prevail on appeal." The court ordered Guardant to pay a 6% royalty on U.S. sales of 11 products and services found to infringe the patents until they expire in March 2033. The judgment includes $83.4 million in original damages, $19.5 million in supplemental damages, $119.4 million in accrued royalties, and $22.9 million in pre- and post-judgment interest. TwinStrand said the products and services covered by the ruling accounted for about 90% of Guardant's revenue during the infringement period. The products covered by the ruling include Guardant360 CDx, Guardant Reveal, the Shield cancer test and several other cancer testing and genomics services sold by Guardant. Guardant had sought to overturn the verdict or obtain a new trial, but the court rejected those efforts, TwinStrand said. The judgment also upheld the validity of the patent claims at issue, TwinStrand said. TwinStrand's Duplex Sequencing technology is designed to detect rare genetic mutations with greater accuracy than conventional DNA sequencing methods. TwinStrand said its technology, developed at the University of Washington, is used in cancer research, diagnostics and drug development.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wirtschaftsstaatssekretär Frank Wetzel hat vor Illusionen bei der Befüllung der Gasspeicher gewarnt. "Staatliche Eingriffe sollten höchst sorgsam überlegt sein, denn sie beeinflussen das Marktgeschehen und damit die Preise", sagte Wetzel am Montag der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters zu Forderungen nach einem staatlichen Eingreifen angesichts der Debatte um den relativ niedrigen Füllstand. "Wo die öffentliche Hand Einspeisung anreizt, nimmt sie Einfluss auf die Nachfrage am Markt und trägt gegebenenfalls zu einem höherem Gaspreisniveau bei", fügte er hinzu. Höhere Speicherfüllstände führten umgekehrt nicht automatisch zu niedrigeren Preisen. Angesichts von Warnungen vor einem zu niedrigen Füllstand der deutschen Gasspeicher betonte Wetzel, dass es keinen Anlass gebe, an der Versorgungssicherheit zu zweifeln. Hintergrund ist, dass die deutschen Gasspeicher in diesem Jahr mit knapp 51 Prozent derzeit weniger befüllt sind als im vergangenen Jahr. 2025 waren es zum gleichen Zeitpunkt 67 Prozent. Der Stromlobbyverband BDEW hatte davor gewarnt, dass es physikalisch "irgendwann" nicht mehr möglich sei, den vorgeschriebenen Füllstand von 70 Prozent bis November zu erreichen. Auch die Bundesnetzagentur hatte sich skeptisch gezeigt, ob die staatliche Vorgabe noch erreicht werden kann. Wetzel erklärte die Zurückhaltung der Gashändler in Deutschland damit, dass sie - anders als im Vorjahr - derzeit weniger erwarteten, dass es zu der typischen Preiserhöhung durch eine erhöhte Winternachfrage komme. "Angesichts der hohen Preise und der Erwartung, dass diese im Winter auf einem ähnlichen Niveau verharren werden, fehlt der normalerweise bestehende betriebswirtschaftliche Anreiz, im Sommer mehr Gas einzuspeichern." Diese "atypische Lage, auch negativer Sommer-Winter-Spread" genannt, behindere zurzeit ein dynamischeres Einspeichergeschehen. Normalerweise können Gashändler im Sommer günstig einkaufen und somit die Speicher füllen, die dann im Winter angezapft werden. Dies ist dieses Jahr aber wegen des Nahost-Krieges, der die Energiepreise nach oben getrieben hat, so nicht möglich. Der Staatssekretär mahnte die Gashändler aber, dass sie ihre Lieferverpflichtungen im Winter zu jeder Zeit erfüllen müssten - auch zu den mit ihren Kunden vereinbarten Bedingungen. Dennoch halte auch das Wirtschaftsministerium ebenso wie die EU-Kommission derzeit die Versorgungslage auch für den Winter für absehbar gesichert. Ein Sprecher des Wirtschaftsministeriums hatte am Vormittag gesagt: "Wir haben einen guten Füllstand in den Speichern." Er hatte unter anderem auf neue Terminals verwiesen, um Flüssiggas (LNG) importieren zu können, sowie auf die Pipeline-Lieferungen aus Norwegen. Im Wirtschaftsministerium wurde auch darauf verwiesen, dass bereits im Koalitionsvertrag vereinbart worden sei, die Füllstandsvorgaben auf den Prüfstand zu stellen. Auch die EU-Kommission fordere eine Überarbeitung der Füllstandsverordnung. Klaus Müller, Präsident der Bundesnetzagentur, hält die Füllvorgaben für Gasspeicher ebenfalls für überholt. "Die Speichervorgaben haben sich in der Krise bewährt, aber inzwischen drohen die Fehlanreize zu überwiegen. Einen Mehrwert sehe ich nicht mehr", sagte er zuletzt der "Zeit". Die Vorgaben stammen aus dem Jahr 2022, als die Gasmärkte wegen Russlands Angriff auf die Ukraine in Panik gerieten. Wetzel verwies darauf, dass das Bundeswirtschaftsministerium mittelfristig eine strategische Gasreserve der öffentlichen Hand aufbauen wolle, die eine verlässliche Reserve für unvorhergesehene Ereignisse darstellen solle, die zu einer Unterversorgung führen könnten. Er mahnte, dass alle Anstrengungen zum Schutz der kritischen Infrastruktur und damit auch der Gasimportwege unternommen werden müssten, um mutwillige Störungen der Versorgung zu unterbinden.

item.title: Tech drags S&P 500, Nasdaq lower as Iran tensions, Nvidia earnings loom
item.description: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq fell on Monday, dragged by technology stocks, while investors assessed the potential fallout from the U.S. pledge of an "economic D-Day" against Iran and looked ahead to Nvidia's earnings and a key inflation report later this week.
item.dc:creator: Purvi Agarwal, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq fell on Monday, dragged by technology stocks, while investors assessed the potential fallout from the U.S. pledge of an "economic D-Day" against Iran and looked ahead to Nvidia's earnings and a key inflation report later this week. The moves mark a sober start to a week that may determine whether equities can shrug off a flare-up in Middle East tensions and worries tied to a tense bond market. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who warned of an "economic D-Day" in an opinion piece published in the Financial Times, is scheduled to hold a press conference in the afternoon. The U.S. has threatened sanctions targeting Iran's trade partners. Chip stocks sold off, with the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index (.SOX) falling 2.64% to its lowest in three weeks. Nvidia (NVDA.O) lost 2.03%, Micron Technology (MU.O) shed 5.76% and Broadcom (AVGO.O) slid 1.74%, pressuring the S&P 500 Information Technology index (.SPLRCT) . Financials (.SPSY) , however, gained 1.19%, with JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) up 1.49% and Visa (V.N) adding 2.64%. They also kept the blue-chip Dow afloat. At 11:55 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 146.59 points, or 0.28%, to 53,423.60. The S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 13.52 points, or 0.18%, to 7,660.85, while the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) fell 99.04 points, or 0.38%, to 26,081.41. EYES ON WARSH'S JACKSON HOLE SPEECH Concerns over ballooning government debt had pushed the 30-year yield to a 19-year high before the Treasury announced support measures last week. CNBC reported on Monday that Bessent could tap Treasury's near $1 trillion General Account to help fund bond buybacks. Yet, the 30-year U.S. Treasury yield remained above the 5% threshold. This turbulence has sharpened focus on Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's speech at the Jackson Hole symposium on Friday, where investors will look for clues on policymakers' reading of the Treasury's rescue efforts. Quarterly results from AI giant Nvidia (NVDA.O) are expected to be another key catalyst for markets. Any sign of slowing growth could reignite concerns over stretched valuations. "Nvidia needs to impress in order to keep one leg of the stock market stable, and Warsh needs to provide clarity on interest rates in order to keep the other leg stable," said Richard Reyle, chief investment officer, Questar Capital Partners. "The Treasury's unprecedented action in the bond market puts Warsh in a tough spot, especially for a Chair that seems to prefer less communication." Markets will also monitor the Personal Consumption Expenditures report, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, due on Wednesday. It will follow a benign consumer inflation report earlier this month that reduced the chances of an immediate increase in interest rates. Traders expect one 25-basis-point hike by the end of 2026, according to LSEG data. Separately, U.S. President Donald Trump warned that tariffs on cars, trucks and automotive parts from Canada would be increased to 50% starting January 1 after trade talks collapsed over the weekend. Automakers Ford (F.N) and General Motors (GM.N) lost 3.9% and 1.9%, respectively, while trucking stocks J.B. Hunt Transport (JBHT.O) slipped about 5.4%. Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.14-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.38-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted 16 new 52-week highs and six new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 62 new highs and 70 new lows.

item.title: How Amazon learned to stop worrying and love arbitration (again)
item.description: Not long ago, mass arbitration loomed as one of corporate America's biggest legal bogeymen.
item.dc:creator: Jenna Greene
item.content:encoded: Not long ago, mass arbitration loomed as one of corporate America's biggest legal bogeymen. "A shakedown," the U.S. Chamber of Commerce called the phenomenon in 2023, describing it as coercive, abusive and a form of blackmail. Today, however, the tactic -- in which attorneys representing consumers flood a company with individual arbitration demands -- appears to be losing some of its punch. Companies and arbitration providers have been rewriting the rules governing mass filings, making it harder for plaintiffs' lawyers to use the prospect of enormous filing fees to force settlements. The clearest sign yet may be Amazon's decision to reinstate mandatory arbitration for customer disputes after a five-year hiatus. As my Reuters colleague Greg Bensinger [USN:L6N44B156 TEXT:"reported"], Amazon changed its conditions of use on Aug. 14, notifying U.S. customers by email that, with limited exceptions, they can no longer sue the company in court. Most disputes must instead proceed through individual arbitration, although small claims cases and pending lawsuits are exempt. Amazon's new rules impose a series of procedural hurdles that plaintiffs' lawyers say could make it economically infeasible to pursue low-value claims on behalf of large groups of consumers with similar grievances. “It’s a huge barrier,” plaintiffs' lawyer Raphael Janove of Janove, who co-chairs the American Association for Justice’s Mass Arbitration Litigation Group, told me. “It effectively makes it impossible to bring mass arbitrations.” An Amazon spokesperson declined to comment on the specifics of the rules but said the return to arbitration “will offer customers a fast, cost-effective way to resolve disputes.” The benefits for Amazon are broader. Arbitration is typically confidential and reduces the risk that claims end up before sympathetic juries. That could prove valuable as Amazon continues to defend personal injury [USN:L1N3X918H TEXT:"lawsuits over allegedly defective products"] sold on its platform, an area where courts have split on the company's liability. TURNING THE TABLES Mass arbitration's original genius was its simplicity. Companies had spent years using arbitration clauses to block class actions, requiring cases to be arbitrated individually. Starting around 2017, however, plaintiffs' lawyers began to [USN:KBN1O52C6 TEXT:"turn the tables"], filing thousands of near-identical arbitration demands at once. The tactic exploited a feature of the system: Defendants were typically obliged to shoulder hefty upfront arbitration filing fees simply to get the process started. Those costs could quickly reach into the tens of millions of dollars, creating enormous pressure to settle regardless of the merits of the claims. The strategy proved so effective that some companies began retreating from arbitration altogether. Amazon did exactly that in 2021 when it scrapped its decade-old requirement that its customers arbitrate disputes. The move came after the company was hit with about 75,000 individual arbitration demands alleging its Alexa voice-assistant software illicitly recorded users. The cases settled for an undisclosed amount. The firm that spearheaded the litigation, Keller Postman, in a 2022 news release , called it an “unprecedented—and astounding” outcome that restored access to the courts for over 140 million Amazon consumers. A Keller spokesperson declined to comment on Amazon’s return to arbitration. According to Amazon’s new conditions of use, dissatisfied consumers can no longer proceed straight to arbitration. Instead, they must first try to resolve their grievance via Amazon customer service. If that fails, the customer must submit a notice of dispute using Amazon’s claim form and negotiate “in good faith” for 60 days before arbitration can commence. These requirements alone are likely to weed out many would-be claimants, plaintiffs' lawyers say, especially if a small amount of money is at stake or the alleged injuries are indirect. Consider a [USN:L6N43X17A TEXT:"proposed class action"] filed in July, before Amazon reinstated mandatory arbitration. The plaintiffs allege Amazon misrepresented the environmental sustainability of seafood sold on its platform. Thousands of consumers who bought products such as canned tuna could potentially be swept into the class. Had the suit been filed after Amazon's rule change, however, how many customers would pursue an individual arbitration? My guess: very few. CAT AND MOUSE For claims against Amazon that make it to arbitration, the proceedings will be administered by Irvine, California-based JAMS, a private arbitration and mediation company. Elizabeth Carter, its senior vice president of operations, told me that JAMS rolled out new procedures for mass arbitrations in 2024. The American Arbitration Association also made similar changes that same year. One key difference is when and how fees are assessed. JAMS now charges a single, flat fee of $8,000 to kick off a mass arbitration, regardless of how many cases are filed. The corporate defendant pays at least $5,500, with the claimants responsible for the balance. Additional fees paid by the defendant accrue as the cases progress. As Carter noted, arbitration is a “creature of contract,” allowing parties to customize their own agreements. Amazon's new mass arbitration protocol applies if 25 or more similar cases are filed within six months by the same lawyers, or by lawyers working in coordination. Amazon also requires that plaintiffs disclose any third-party litigation funding. A JAMS process administrator then groups the cases in “batches” decided by a single arbitrator. Plaintiffs' lawyer Caleb Marker, a partner at Zimmerman Reed in Los Angeles, describes the process as “a procedural morass," adding, "it’s just that Amazon prefers this procedural morass over class actions, probably after an internal cost-benefit analysis.” Still, Amazon’s new rules are likely not the final word on the viability of mass arbitration. For example, Vanderbilt Law School professor Brian Fitzpatrick, an expert in class action litigation, said the batch provisions could be vulnerable to a court challenge, including over whether the procedures as laid out actually fall within the definition of “arbitration” under the Federal Arbitration Act of 1925. “It’s a cat and mouse game,” Fitzpatrick told me, with each side “shifting in response to what the other side did last.” Five years ago, Amazon determined that the courtroom was the better option. The company’s return to arbitration suggests that calculus has changed. The question now is how long it may take plaintiffs' lawyers to change it again.

item.title: Britain, France pledge stronger support as Ukraine marks Independence Day
item.description: The leaders of Britain and France pledged to provide Ukraine with stronger military support — including access to classified technology and faster deliveries of air defence missiles — at a meeting of allies to mark Kyiv's independence day celebrations.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Anna Pruchnicka
item.content:encoded: The leaders of Britain and France pledged to provide Ukraine with stronger military support — including access to classified technology and faster deliveries of air defence missiles — at a meeting of allies to mark Kyiv's independence day celebrations. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, in Kyiv on his first foreign visit since taking office last month, urged the gathering of the "Coalition of the Willing" to "do everything we can" to bolster Ukraine's defences against Russian air strikes. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy had earlier praised the resilience of the Ukrainian people during more than four years of war. UKRAINE GETS TECH TO MAKE STORM SHADOW MISSILES "Ukraine absolutely wants peace, but it is not ready to simply surrender," Zelenskiy said, adding that Russia would not halt its aggression even if Ukraine ceded to its demands for more territory in the country's east. Wearing a traditional Ukrainian embroidered shirt, Zelenskiy thanked foreign leaders for travelling to Kyiv to show their support on the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's break from the Soviet Union. Standing alongside Zelenskiy and European Council President Antonio Costa, Burnham said his choice of Kyiv for his first foreign visit showed the importance he attached to assisting in Ukraine's defence. "We are with you in this struggle all the way, heart and soul," Burnham said, vowing to continue that support "despite Russia's outrageous threats to my country." "This is the moment to keep up the pressure on Russia. The moment to squeeze their ability to fund this illegal war," Burnham said, calling for further economic sanctions. Britain announced on Monday it would allow Kyiv access to classified technology to start its own production of Storm Shadow long-range cruise missiles, capable of carrying out strikes deep within Russia. France has already given its assent to license the technology for the European missile. In response, the Kremlin said the use of classified British technology would "add fuel to the fire" of their worsening relations, after it warned London last week there would be "consequences" for supplying drones to Kyiv. UKRAINE NEEDS MORE INTERCEPTORS, PRESIDENT SAYS With Russia escalating its ballistic missile attacks on Ukrainian cities, Kyiv is suffering an acute shortage of the U.S.-made Patriot air defence interceptors — the only weapon in its arsenal capable of downing such missiles. Zelenskiy said Ukraine needed at least 300 interceptors to make it through the winter, and he appealed to allies to deliver an air defence package before Russia renews its strikes on his country's energy infrastructure. French President Emmanuel Macron, co-chairing the coalition meeting via video link, said that a string of deadly attacks on Ukrainian cities in recent weeks had shown that allies needed to step up the deliveries of interceptors and France would do its part. "I think it's very important that all of us accelerate in terms of delivery," Macron told the meeting, urging countries not to back down in the face of Russian intimidation. "The bottom line is, for me, very clear: keep calm and carry on." Zelenskiy told the meeting that Ukraine's war effort was complicated by a [USN:L1N44K01P TEXT:"$27-billion defence funding gap"] this year and appealed for additional financial support. He suggested that Russia's frozen overseas assets could be used to finance the deficit. Paying tribute to Ukrainian people and soldiers defending Ukraine in the war, Zelenskiy called on allies to give it "everything" needed to stop the war. "We are not asking you to fight for us," he said. DRONE DEMONSTRATION Hundreds of thousands of people have been killed, and swathes of Ukrainian territory have been laid waste, since Russia launched its full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022. U.S.-led peace talks to bring a lasting end to the war fell apart earlier this year as Ukraine refused Russian demands to cede more territory. Fighting continues along a 750-mile (1,200-km) front line and Ukraine has succeeded in bringing Russian advances overall to a virtual halt this year. Hovering in the sky above Kyiv, a squadron of aerial drones carried out a demonstration of the Ukrainian military technology, which has helped to keep Russian forces in check. Naval drones swept along the Dnipro river, while unmanned ground vehicles — some equipped with heavy machine guns — trundled in formation along one of the city's main historical avenues. Ukraine has increased its long-range attacks on Russian refineries and logistics infrastructure, aimed at undermining Moscow's war effort. It hit four logistics hubs owned by Russia's second-largest online retailer Ozon in southern Russia in drone strikes on Monday, the company said. In a sombre moment, the Ukrainian leader rewarded fallen soldiers with state awards, which he presented to their mothers and family members. He also announced the return of 10 Ukrainian servicemen, who were previously listed as missing in action, as part of a special prisoner exchange with Russia. "We remember each and every one who remains in captivity," Zelenskiy said, promising to do everything possible to bring them home.

item.title: California cancels talks with Paramount over Warner Bros deal
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta canceled a meeting with Paramount Skydance representatives scheduled for Monday to begin settlement talks over the state's lawsuit seeking to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery , his office said.
item.dc:creator: Jody Godoy
item.content:encoded: California Attorney General Rob Bonta canceled a meeting with Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) representatives scheduled for Monday to begin settlement talks over the state's lawsuit seeking to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD.O) , his office said. Paramount has pushed for a settlement in the case, as it faces a [USN:FWN44E0IP TEXT:"mountain of fees and costs"] to keep the deal together if the lawsuit continues to a trial scheduled for March. Bonta and his partner states have so far won key rulings, giving them leverage if settlement talks continue. Bonta accused Paramount of leaking details of a meeting held on Friday and acting in bad faith. "Not only did Paramount leak the alleged substance of settlement discussions, but they misrepresented these discussions, demonstrating a lack of good faith," Bonta said, adding his office met with Paramount on Friday. "As soon as Paramount stops playing games and engages sincerely, my office is happy to meet again," Bonta added. A Paramount spokesperson declined to comment. Bonta has repeatedly indicated an openness to settling cases generally. But he has also said that [USN:L6N42C19I TEXT:"structural remedies"], which could include selling off part of a business, are better than companies promising to take actions. Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison has promised to release 30 movies per year and to keep them exclusively in theaters for 45 days. California and 11 [USN:L6N42C19I TEXT:"states sued on July 13"], arguing the deal would create a media behemoth with the power to raise prices in film and television. The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday that Bonta planned to ask Paramount to divest some cable channels and commit to keeping its movie studio separate from Warner Bros. before he signs off on their merger, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: European stocks flat as markets weigh Iran tensions, await economic data
item.description: European shares were flat on Monday as markets monitored U.S.-Iran developments and looked ahead to a busy week of economic data that could offer fresh clues on the European Central Bank's policy path.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Utkarsh Hathi
item.content:encoded: European shares were flat on Monday as markets monitored U.S.-Iran developments and looked ahead to a busy week of economic data that could offer fresh clues on the European Central Bank's policy path. Investors braced for details of potentially tougher U.S. secondary [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"sanctions"] on countries with trade ties to Iran, expected to be announced by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Separately, Pakistan's army chief is in Tehran to bring Iran back to the negotiating table. "There are a lot of unknowns riding on this (sanctions) at the moment," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst, IG Group. "If you have a situation where the U.S. action is taken as a threat to the Iranian economy and they respond in the only way they can and then take action in the Strait of Hormuz, it would be particularly bad for European markets." The pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) closed unchanged at 654.21 points. The threat of sanctions follows fears of prolonged inflation that gripped global markets last week as U.S. Treasury yields hit a multi-decade high amid persisting tensions in the Middle East that have kept oil prices elevated. Among sectors, energy-intensive travel and leisure stocks (.SXTP) led gains, rising 1.7% as Brent crude declined 1.9%. Media (.SXPP) and personal and household goods shares (.SXQP) rose 1.4%. The benchmark STOXX 600 has pulled back in recent weeks after reaching record highs earlier this month on an earnings-fuelled rally with inflation concerns taking centre stage. Money markets are pricing in a more [USN:L1N44L06D TEXT:"hawkish move from the European Central Bank"], betting geopolitical tensions could keep price pressures elevated and drive the deposit rate close to 3% by late 2027. Investors are also awaiting a string of economic releases this week, including German and French GDP data, the German Ifo survey and Spanish inflation figures, that could test expectations for a more hawkish ECB amid renewed pressure from energy prices. Energy (.SXEP) fell 1.6%, tracking oil, to be the worst-performing sector. Defence stocks (.SXPARO) also slipped 1%. Automobiles and parts (.SXAP) fell 1% despite data showing [USN:L1N44A0H2 TEXT:"European EV sales picked up"] in July. Meanwhile, the tech sector (.SX8P) slipped 0.8% ahead of Nvidia's (NVDA.O) results on Wednesday, with lingering concerns about whether the chipmaker can meet stratospheric expectations.

item.title: Video appears to show 600 people abducted in Nigeria mosque attack, residents say
item.description: An armed group has posted a video showing what residents said were about 600 women, children and older people abducted in an attack on a mosque in Nigeria’s north-central Niger State last week.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Kingimi, Hamza Ibrahim
item.content:encoded: An armed group has posted a video showing what residents said were about 600 women, children and older people abducted in [USN:L6N44J02S TEXT:"an attack"] on a mosque in Nigeria’s north-central Niger State last week. The video, posted on Sunday on Facebook and WhatsApp, showed large groups of people seated in a forested area surrounded by armed men. Several children could be heard crying in the background. Mass kidnappings for ransom have become common in parts of northwestern and north-central Nigeria, where heavily armed gangs frequently raid villages, schools and highways and hold them until paid large sums of money. Gunmen have increasingly [USN:L8N42C13S TEXT:"expanded south"], beyond hotspots in the north. 'WE HAVE IDENTIFIED OUR ELDERS, RELATIVES' The video surfaced two days after the latest kidnapping when gunmen attacked worshippers at the mosque in Dekara village during Friday prayers, taking people away in what residents said were simultaneous raids on several communities. In the video, a gunman speaking in Hausa addressed families of the captives and urged them to identify relatives among the people in the footage. "These are all your people. We are showing you this video so that you can identify your family members, your fathers, mothers, children and relatives," the gunman said. Reuters could not verify the exact date or the location where the video was filmed. However, no older version of the video was found posted online before August 23, 2026. Four residents said they were able to confirm the identities of some of those seized. "The people in the video are from Dekara. I've identified 13 people that I know," Ibrahim Abubakar told Reuters. Another resident, Abdulmutallib Muqaddas Dindi, said those who appeared in the video had been seized during the prayers. "We have identified our elders, relatives, and some of us have seen their wives and children in the video," he said. Police and state authorities did not respond to requests for comment on Monday. Police had earlier confirmed an attack on worshippers in the area but said they could not verify the number of people abducted. Resident Jamilu Ibrahim appealed to federal and state authorities to secure the release of the captives, pointing out the number of mothers with infants and children among those shown in the footage.

item.title: Norway asks supreme court to overturn environmental verdict against oilfields
item.description: Norway's government on Monday asked the country's supreme court to overturn a lower-court ruling that invalidated permits for three oilfields, in a closely watched case that could reshape how the country approves new petroleum projects.
item.dc:creator: Terje Solsvik, Gwladys Fouche
item.content:encoded: Norway's government on Monday asked the country's supreme court to overturn a lower-court ruling that invalidated permits for three oilfields, in a closely watched case that could reshape how the country approves new petroleum projects. The case pits environmental groups against Norway's oil industry, provider of half the country's export revenue, as well as the government whose policy is to [USN:L8N44I0B4 TEXT:"prolong the extraction"] of crude and natural gas for decades to come. Two lower courts have [USN:L8N3WQ1LQ TEXT:"ruled in favour"] of Greenpeace and Young Friends of the Earth since the two groups first brought the case to trial in 2023, finding that Norway failed to properly assess the environmental impact from the three fields. "If we win this round, it could change Norwegian oil politics forever," Haldis Tjeldflaat Helle, leader of Greenpeace Norway, told Reuters outside the court. "It means that Norwegian politicians will have to actually assess how many lives will be lost, how many forest fires will be created and how much ice will melt due to Norwegian oil." The case concerns Equinor's (EQNR.OL) Breidablikk and Aker BP's (AKRBP.OL) Tyrving and Yggdrasil fields, of which the first two are already in production while the third is due to come on stream next year. The green campaigners argue that the government failed to consider the climate impact of the burning of the fields' oil and gas, known as Scope 3 emissions, and that efforts to rectify this at a later stage were invalid. ENERGY SECURITY AT STAKE, GOVERNMENT SAYS But the lower courts have declined to order a halt to production while the legal process is ongoing, and have also suggested that the government could seek to remedy regulatory shortcomings. "The government's position is of course that the licences are valid," Fredrik Sejersted, Norway's attorney general, told Reuters ahead of the hearing. "If they should be overturned then it will be quite complicated," he said. "Legally, politically and for energy security in Europe." Norway produces around 2% of global oil and became Europe's largest supplier of natural gas after Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, making it a crucial provider of energy. The supreme court hearing is set to run for four days, and a verdict in the case is expected sometime later this year.

item.title: Coach carrying German high-school students crashes in Netherlands
item.description: A coach carrying high-school students from Germany crashed in the east of the Netherlands early on Monday, injuring 16 people who were taken to hospital, Dutch police said.
item.dc:creator: Christian Levaux
item.content:encoded: A coach carrying high-school students from Germany crashed in the east of the Netherlands early on Monday, injuring 16 people who were taken to hospital, Dutch police said. Eight of those hurt have been severely wounded and the others suffered minor injuries, the police department of Gelderland province said in a post on X. The coach, which was carrying more than 50 people and was registered in Austria, according to a police spokesperson, crashed near the town of Wezep, some 100 km (62 miles) east of Amsterdam around 4 a.m. (0200 GMT) due to a collision with a delivery van, whose driver was among the injured. The A28 highway was closed in both directions following the accident.

item.title: Gold rally gains momentum ahead of US inflation data, Jackson Hole event
item.description: Gold prices rose to their highest in more than three months on Monday, as technical buyers piled into a rally driven by the U.S. Treasury's recent buyback announcement and a weaker dollar ahead of this week's inflation data and the Jackson Hole Symposium.
item.dc:creator: Dharna Bafna
item.content:encoded: Gold prices rose to their highest in more than three months on Monday, as technical buyers piled into a rally driven by the U.S. Treasury's recent buyback announcement and a weaker dollar ahead of this week's inflation data and the Jackson Hole Symposium. Spot gold rose 1.5% to $4,673.20 per ounce by 1535 GMT (11:35 a.m. EDT), its highest level since May 14. U.S. gold futures for December delivery rose 1.1% to $4,730.40 per ounce. "The fundamentals and technicals are kind of lining up bullish for the gold market here to start the trading week," said Jim Wyckoff, a market analyst at American Gold Exchange. He also said that bond yields "have stabilized, even dipped a little bit today", supporting the metal. With prices trending higher, Wyckoff said the path of least resistance for gold "will continue to be sideways to higher" in the coming weeks, barring a technical reversal signal. Gold broke above its 200-day moving average last week, further strengthening the upward price momentum. Gold-backed ETFs also attracted inflows of 46.7 metric tons ($6.4 billion) last week, which was their largest weekly demand in 10 months, according to the World Gold Council, with North American and Europe-listed funds leading the inflows. Bullion rose more than 5% last week after the U.S. Treasury Department's [USN:L1N44H0P5 TEXT:"buyback support plan"] pushed the dollar to [USN:L6N44L0JB TEXT:"multi-month lows"], making greenback-priced bullion cheaper for foreign buyers. The U.S. dollar hovered near multi-month lows as traders awaited details on Iran-related sanctions from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. He is expected to announce [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"more details"] at a press conference at 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT). Market focus is also on policy speeches this week in the U.S. and Japan. Markets are awaiting the Personal Consumption Expenditure price index, the Federal Reserve's favored inflation gauge, due on Wednesday and Chair Kevin Warsh's debut speech at the Jackson Hole Symposium on Friday to understand the outlook on interest rates. Spot silver inched 0.2% up to $69.06 per ounce, platinum gained 0.8% to $1,892.03, and palladium rose 1.8% to $1,374.27.

item.title: Shares dip on pressure from technology; yields and oil fall
item.description: MSCI's global equities gauge was lower on Monday as weakness in technology stocks offset support from a dip in U.S. Treasury yields and falling oil prices.
item.dc:creator: Sinead Carew, Iain Withers
item.content:encoded: MSCI's global equities gauge was lower on Monday as weakness in technology stocks offset support from a dip in U.S. Treasury yields and falling oil prices. Investors were waiting for details of threatened [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"U.S. sanctions"] on Iran with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent due to hold a press conference later on Monday to outline the details. [USN:L1N44L0IK TEXT:"Treasury yields"] fell following a report that the Treasury Department may tap its cash account to finance increased debt buybacks. In currencies, the [USN:L6N44J03R TEXT:"Canadian dollar"] dipped due to a looming U.S. trade war. While most of the S&P 500's industry sectors were gaining ground, heavyweight technology led losses in a handful of declining sectors. "Today it's a mixed bag. Technology is being dragged down by the overnight news from two key companies, but the rest of the market is reacting positively to lower oil prices and lower bond yields," said Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera, El Segundo, CA. In particular Goldman pointed to Alibaba's (9988.HK) , launch of a [USN:L6N44L021 TEXT:"$10.2 billion share sale"] at a steep discount to fund its AI ambitions. And South Korean shares fell after [USN:L1N44L074 TEXT:"Samsung Electronics"] (005930.KS) announced a $79 billion shareholder-return plan, which was a record but still smaller than the windfall its investors had expected. Technology investors were already on edge ahead of Nvidia's (NVDA.O) quarterly financial report on Wednesday with worries about how hard it will be for the leading AI chipmaker to meet sky-high expectations. On Monday at 11:14 a.m. ET (1514 GMT), the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 89.04 points, or 0.17%, to 53,361.60, the S&P 500 (.SPX) fell 28.66 points, or 0.37%, to 7,645.71 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) fell 186.77 points, or 0.71%, to 25,993.69. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe (.MIWD00000PUS) fell 5.02 points, or 0.44%, to 1,144.79 while the pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) index fell 0.01%. Earlier South Korea's KOSPI index (.KS11) finished down more than 3%. FROM JACKSON HOLE TO TRADE WARS Also coming up this week is [USN:L6N44L0MM TEXT:"Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's first speech"] at an annual conference in Jackson Hole. The appearance has taken on added weight as traders and analysts look for guidance about the recent jump in bond yields and for reassurance of his independence from the Trump administration. While traders are pricing in a roughly 60% probability that the Fed will hold rates steady at its September meeting, the expectation is for at least one hike by December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. In government bonds, the yield on benchmark U.S. 10-year notes fell 3.99 basis points to 4.698%, from 4.738% late on Friday, while the 30-year bond yield fell 4.94 basis points to 5.2266%. The 2-year note yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, fell 0.46 basis point to 4.229%. U.S.-CANADIAN TRADE WAR Currency markets were impacted by U.S.-Canada trade tensions. President Donald Trump said in a social media post on Monday, after trade talks with Canada collapsed over the weekend, that tariffs on all cars and trucks, automotive parts and steel will be increased to 50% starting on January 1, 2027. The Canadian dollar weakened 0.48% versus the greenback to C$1.383 per dollar while Prime Minister [USN:L6N44J03R TEXT:"Mark Carney"] said his country would respond to U.S. tariffs with levies of its own. The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.15% to 98.96, with the euro down 0.1% at $1.1667. Against the Japanese yen , the dollar strengthened 0.13% to 159.13. In [USN:L1N44K05C TEXT:"energy markets"], U.S. crude fell 2.37% to $85.00 a barrel and Brent fell to $92.65 per barrel, down 1.83% on the day. In [USN:L6N44L0MZ TEXT:"precious metals"], gold prices pushed to their highest levels in more than three months as technical buyers piled into a rally driven by the U.S. Treasury's recent buyback announcement and a weaker dollar ahead of this week's inflation data and the Jackson Hole meeting. Spot gold rose 1.53% to $4,673.16 an ounce. U.S. gold futures rose 1.01% to $4,670.90 an ounce.

item.title: Oil slips ahead of US announcement of new sanctions on Iran
item.description: Brent crude futures fell to $93.45.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Jao
item.content:encoded: Oil prices fell more than $2 a barrel on Monday as investors took profits after recent gains and awaited details of expected new U.S. sanctions on Iran , which could further disrupt supplies from the Middle East. Brent crude futures were down $1.71, or 1.81%, to $92.69 at 12:48 p.m. ET (1648 GMT), while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was at $85.34 a barrel, down $1.72, or 1.98%. Both contracts posted a second consecutive weekly gain last week, rising more than 5%, as peace negotiations between the U.S. and Iran stalled, constraining oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, a route that once carried a fifth of global supplies. U.S. Treasury Secretary [USN:L1N44K02A TEXT:"Scott Bessent"], who is set to hold a press conference at 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT) on Monday, is expected to outline measures to broaden the scope of potential secondary sanctions on entities and countries that maintain economic ties with Iran. President Donald Trump has also threatened to impose sanctions on Iran's trading partners. "Should the pledged embargo be launched, oil supply from the region will fall," said PVM analyst Tamas Varga, adding that the U.S. would likely tighten its naval blockade against Iranian oil exports and that Iran could retaliate with fresh strikes against oil installations in the Middle East. Iran has condemned U.S. plans to announce new sanctions and President Masoud Pezeshkian has called for a [USN:L6N44J01G TEXT:"diplomatic solution"]. Pakistan's [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"army chief was visiting Tehran"] on Monday for mediation talks, ahead of the U.S. announcement. Fewer than 20 commodity vessels [USN:L1N44L01G TEXT:"transited"] the Strait of Hormuz at the weekend, shipping data showed on Monday, as Iranian and U.S. blockades restrict traffic through the chokepoint for energy shipments. TotalEnergies Chief Executive Patrick Pouyanne said (TTEF.PA) the oil company was profitably moving oil through the Strait of Hormuz, with higher transport costs more than offset by steep discounts from crude producers. Iraq's SOMO and QatarEnergy both [USN:L1N44L03O TEXT:"offered crude for loading inside the strait"] in tenders, traders said. "$93 per barrel Brent, rather than $120-150, is telling us that enough oil is flowing through the Strait of Hormuz and from the Persian Gulf in general," SEB analyst Bjarne Schieldrop told Reuters, adding that a turning point could be if Iran decided to actually close Hormuz with rockets and drones. Morgan Stanley analysts have [USN:L6N44L0HG TEXT:"increased their Brent forecasts"], projecting a peak of $100 per barrel in the fourth quarter. The International Energy Agency is not currently discussing a second release of oil from strategic reserves, its chief Fatih Birol said on Monday.

item.title: US expected to broaden secondary sanctions to isolate Iran on 'economic D-Day'
item.description: The United States was set to warn countries to cut ties with Iran or risk their businesses being cut off from the dollar-based financial system when it unveils the "greatest financial offensive ever" on Monday, a source told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, Asif Shahzad, Ariba Shahid
item.content:encoded: The United States was set to warn countries to cut ties with Iran or risk their businesses being cut off from the dollar-based financial system when it unveils the "greatest financial offensive ever" on Monday, a source told Reuters. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will outline measures at 1 p.m. (1700 GMT) to broaden the scope of potential secondary sanctions on entities and countries that maintain economic ties with Iran, said the source, who was familiar with the plans but not authorized to speak publicly. The move is part of U.S. efforts to put pressure on Iran to end the attacks on ships in the Gulf and, more recently via its allies, in the Red Sea, that Tehran launched after the U.S. and Israel began air strikes against it in February. Iran has said it will have the opposite effect. Bessent [USN:L6N44H0X1 TEXT:"previously urged cooperation from China"], the biggest buyer of Iranian oil for several years, although the U.S. blockade of Iran's ports, renewed in mid-July, has already [USN:L4N44L0FN TEXT:"cut Iranian oil flows"] to China. But experts say Washington is wary of Chinese retaliation for any sanctions on its banks ahead of expected talks next month between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, with any curbs on China's exports of critical minerals especially sensitive. The Chinese foreign ministry said sanctions and pressure tactics do not help and that Beijing would do what was necessary to protect China's interests. PAKISTAN'S ARMY CHIEF HOLDS TALKS ON IRAN Bessent may sharpen enforcement against oil shippers, purchasers and currency exchangers who help Iran pay for its imports. He could also target aviation. Trump has threatened tariffs on goods from [USN:L6N44H0PZ TEXT:"countries doing business with Iran"], which include Turkey, Iraq and India, although the Supreme Court struck down the legal basis for such taxes. Iran has dismissed the U.S. threat and issued a [USN:L1N44L07X TEXT:"new warning to shipping"] not to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without its permission, listing 45 ships it said had violated its rules and[USN:L6N44L0PO TEXT:" threatening retaliation"] for any ship-to-ship transfers with them. Bessent wrote in the Financial Times that Monday would mark "an economic D-Day — the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary". Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir, who has built a personal rapport with Trump, was in Iran on Monday for talks, Iranian media said. Pakistan said the visit aimed "to promote regional peace and stability", and a Pakistani source said Munir would meet people close to Iran's supreme leader. Two Pakistani sources said Trump had called Munir last week, with another saying the main request was to [USN:L1N44L090 TEXT:"bring Iran back to negotiations"]. The White House confirmed the call but did not comment on its substance. Posting on Telegram after the meeting with Munir, Iran's top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf said commitments made by both sides in a June preliminary accord were clear. The U.S. through bad faith hindered the establishment of stability in the region and created another reason for distrust towards that country, he wrote. PROJECTILE HITS TANKER NEAR SAUDI RED SEA PORT, MONITORS SAY The U.S. and Iran have not conducted air strikes on each other's militaries for weeks, but their last official face-to-face talks to end the six-month-old conflict took place in June and strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz have continued. A projectile [USN:L1N44L08M TEXT:"struck a tanker"] west of the Saudi port city of Yanbu in the Red Sea on Monday, causing a fire on the main deck, shipping monitors from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said. A spokesperson for Iran's Houthi allies, who last month [USN:L1N43M0DO TEXT:"announced they would block"] Saudi oil exports diverted to the Red Sea to avoid Hormuz, said they had attacked a vessel in the area. Saudi Arabia's national shipping company confirmed that one of its vessels had been attacked. Thousands of people have died, most of them in Iran and Lebanon, since the U.S. and Israel began strikes on February 28, degrading much of Iran's conventional military capacity and inflicting economic pain while killing [USN:L6N43B0GV TEXT:"Iran's then-Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei"]. Yet Iran has continued to attack its Gulf neighbours and keep shipping in the Strait of Hormuz at [USN:L1N44L01G TEXT:"a near standstill"], pushing up world fuel prices. The exact state of its nuclear program, which the Americans and Israelis aim to wipe out, remains unknown. Oil prices [USN:L1N44K05C TEXT:"eased"] on Monday after two weeks of gains as investors took profits ahead of the expected U.S. announcement. Iran has been bracing for the sanctions for days, issuing a series of statements hinting at a major military response. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on Sunday further penalties would simply trigger a tighter squeeze on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran entered the war with high inflation and energy shortages and must now contend with disrupted trade, lost production and the cost of rebuilding damaged infrastructure. A slide in the rial currency, which prompted protests in January that were violently suppressed, [USN:S8N42206W TEXT:"reached a new record low"] on Monday, 25% below its January level.

item.title: Video de derrumbe de edificio fue grabado en Colombia y antecede a terremoto en Perú
item.description: Un video que muestra el derrumbe de una parte de un edificio en Pereira, Colombia, se comparte erróneamente en publicaciones como si se tratara de un registro del sismo de magnitud 7.2 que impactó a Perú el 20 de agosto.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Un video que muestra el derrumbe de una parte de un edificio en Pereira, Colombia, se comparte erróneamente en publicaciones como si se tratara de un registro del sismo de magnitud 7.2 que impactó a Perú el 20 de agosto. Estos son los detalles clave: Algunos ejemplos en línea con el video dicen que es un registro del terremoto en agosto en Perú. Una de las versiones más antiguas y con mayor interacción que comparte el clip fue publicada por la página Pereira Elige el 19 de agosto, un día antes del sismo . La descripción dice el video muestra el colapso de una vivienda familiar y que las personas que estaban en él sobrevivieron. Los responsables de la página dijeron el 21 de agosto por correo electrónico que recibieron el video por WhatsApp y que el inmueble está en la ciudad. Imágenes de Google Street View también muestran el edificio. La usuaria @angie43lopez comentó en la publicación que el hombre que grabó el video es su primo y que su familia está a salvo. En un mensaje de Instagram el 21 de agosto, la usuaria dijo a Reuters que el video fue grabado el 10 de agosto y compartió imágenes adicionales del interior y exterior de la vivienda. El 10 de agosto, un sismo de [USN:L1N3AC29B TEXT:"magnitud 7.4"] dejó al menos 321 muertos en Colombia. Reuters no pudo verificar independientemente la fecha de grabación del video. La Policía Metropolitana de Pereira y la Policía Nacional de Perú no respondieron a solicitudes de comentarios. Veredicto: Erróneamente etiquetado. El video fue grabado en Pereira, Colombia, no muestra el derrumbe de un edificio durante el sismo que impactó Perú el 20 de agosto. item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: L'Europe termine sur une note prudente, en attendant des annonces américaines
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Europe termine sur une note prudente, en attendant des annonces américaines 24 août (Reuters) - Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en baisse mardi, dans l'attente de précisions de la part des États-Unis sur plusieurs catalyseurs aussi bien géopolitiques que macroéconomiques. La "guerre de Trump" à l'origine de la flambée des taux obligataires - ministre allemand BERLIN, 24 août (Reuters) - La récente flambée des taux obligataires est le résultat de "la guerre menée par le président américain Donald Trump en Iran", a déclaré lundi le ministre allemand des Finances Lars Klingbeil, lors d'une conférence de presse à Schaan, au Liechtenstein. Trump menace d'imposer des droits de douane de 50% sur les véhicules produits au Canada WASHINGTON, 24 août (Reuters) - Les droits de douane américains sur les voitures, les camions, les pièces détachées automobiles et l'acier produits au Canada seront portés à 50% à compter du 1er janvier 2027, a déclaré lundi Donald Trump dans un message publié sur les réseaux sociaux après l'échec des négociations commerciales avec Ottawa. Les valeurs à suivre à Wall Street Principales valeurs à suivre lundi à Wall Street, où les contrats à terme sur les principaux indices suggèrent une ouverture stable (-0,01%) pour le Dow Jones <.DJI>, en baisse de 0,12% pour le Standard & Poor's-500 <.SPX> et de 0,49% pour le Nasdaq. Jackson Hole: Le premier discours de Warsh sous surveillance avec l'agitation sur l'obligataire WASHINGTON, 24 août (Reuters) - Le discours de Kevin Warsh, président de la Réserve fédérale américaine (Fed), lors de la conférence de Jackson Hole qui débute cette semaine, suscitera sans aucun doute un intérêt allant bien au-delà de l'évidence, à un moment où le marché cherche des éclaircissements sur la récente flambée des rendements obligataires et des garanties quant à l'indépendance de la banque centrale. Le milliardaire allemand Klaus-Michael Kuehne s'éteint à l'âge de 89 ans Le milliardaire allemand Klaus-Michael Kuehne, actionnaire majoritaire du groupe logistique suisse Kuehne+Nagel, est décédé à l'âge de 89 ans, a annoncé lundi la société. Volkswagen: Les salariés inquiets de la communication du directoire BERLIN, 24 août (Reuters) - Les salariés de Volkswagen ont critiqué ce qu’ils ont qualifié de "communication externe désastreuse" de la part du directoire, alors que le plus grand constructeur automobile européen envisage de nouvelles réductions de coûts, selon un article interne du comité d’entreprise consulté lundi par Reuters. Shein pourrait atteindre une valorisation de $27 mds lors de son IPO à Hong Kong HONG KONG, 24 août (Reuters) - La valorisation de Shein a chuté d'environ 70% par rapport au pic de près de 100 milliards de dollars atteint lors d'un tour de table effectué il y a quatre ans, alors que le géant en ligne chinois de la mode éphémère entend lever jusqu'à 1,77 milliards de dollars en vue de son introduction en Bourse à Hong Kong. Shell: Les actifs chimiques américains suscitent l'intérêt d'Exxon et LyondellBasell selon le Financial Times 24 août (Reuters) - Shell a suscité l'intérêt de plusieurs acquéreurs potentiels, dont ExxonMobil et LyondellBasell, pour ses actifs chimiques américains, qui pourraient atteindre une valeur de 8 milliards de dollars (6,85 milliards d'euros), a rapporté lundi le Financial Times (FT). Le Vatican va construire une centrale agrivoltaïque à €100 mlns - sources Le Vatican va construire une centrale agrivoltaïque qui pourrait alimenter le Saint-Siège en électricité d'origine renouvelable d'ici deux ans, ont déclaré des sources impliquées dans les discussions sur le projet.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Deux casques bleus de l'ONU tués dans une embuscade dans l'Etat du Jonglei NAIROBI, 24 août (Reuters) - Deux casques bleus de l'ONU ont été tués lundi lors d'une embuscade lors d'une patrouille dans l'État du Jonglei, au Soudan du Sud, a déclaré la mission de l'ONU dans un communiqué. Lula et Flavio Bolsonaro au coude à coude à l'approche des élections brésiliennes - sondage Nexus SÃO PAULO, 24 août (Reuters) - L'avance du président brésilien de gauche Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sur le sénateur de droite Flavio Bolsonaro dans un éventuel second tour des élections présidentielles d'octobre s'est quasiment évanouie, les deux hommes se retrouvant à un point d'écart, selon un sondage Nexus commandé par la banque BTG Pactual, publié lundi. Les Houthis revendiquent l'attaque d'un navire au large de l'Arabie saoudite LE CAIRE, 24 août (Reuters) - Les Houthis yéménites, proches de l'Iran, ont attaqué un navire au large de la ville portuaire saoudienne de Yanbu, en mer Rouge, a déclaré lundi le porte-parole militaire du groupe, Yahya Saree, lors d'un discours télévisé. L'Ukraine veut la paix, mais ne se soumettra pas, dit Zelensky KYIV, 24 août (Reuters) - L'Ukraine veut la paix mais elle ne se soumettra jamais à la Russie, a déclaré lundi le président Volodimir Zelensky dans un discours pugnace prononcé à l'occasion du 35e anniversaire de l'Indépendance de son pays. Taïwan: Neuf personnes inculpées pour avoir exporté des serveurs d'IA vers la Chine TAIPEI, 24 août (Reuters) - Le parquet taïwanais a annoncé lundi avoir mis en examen neuf personnes, dont des employés de Nvidia et de Super Micro, accusées d'avoir exporté illégalement vers la Chine des serveurs d'intelligence artificielle (IA). La Nouvelle-Zélande veut interdire l'accès aux réseaux sociaux aux moins de 16 ans SYDNEY, 24 août (Reuters) - Le Premier ministre néo-zélandais, Christopher Luxon, a déclaré lundi que son parti allait présenter au Parlement un projet de loi visant à interdire aux enfants de moins de 16 ans d'utiliser les réseaux sociaux, la Nouvelle-Zélande étant le dernier pays en date à vouloir prendre des mesures en la matière. Taïwan sous des pluies torrentielles, quatre personnes portées disparues TAIPEI, 24 août (Reuters) - Quatre personnes sont portées disparues après que des pluies torrentielles se sont abattues lundi sur le sud et l'est de Taïwan, entraînant la fermeture des bureaux et des écoles. Thaïlande: Des séparatistes soupçonnés d'incendies criminels dans le sud selon les autorités BANGKOK, 24 août (Reuters) - Des bâtiments administratifs, des commerces, des voitures et des poteaux électriques ont été incendiés au cours du week-end par des insurgés présumés, dans plus de 70 localités réparties dans quatre des provinces les plus au sud de la Thaïlande, blessant au moins trois personnes, ont déclaré lundi les autorités. Discussions Syrie-Israël de désescalade chapeautées par les USA 24 août (Reuters) - La Syrie et Israël ont pris part dimanche en Jordanie à des discussions à haut niveau chapeautées par les Etats-Unis destinées à apaiser les tensions entre les deux voisins à la suite des bombardements effectués par l'Etat hébreu en territoire syrien, a rapporté la presse officielle syrienne. Zelensky juge que des élections en temps de guerre détruiraient l'Ukraine Organiser des élections en Ukraine en temps de guerre, sans cessation majeure des hostilités, détruirait le pays en fracturant la société, a estimé le président Volodimir Zelensky devant des journalistes, sa première réponse à l'appel aux urnes lancé par son ancien ministre de la Défense Mykhaïlo Fedorov.
